summary: No verifiable fresh signal today. Every free-source result repeated the 1 July NSW reform package already captured across the 28 June - 10 August digests: the psychological-injury 'relevant event' compensability test requiring a real and direct connection to employment with employment as the main contributing factor, the staged Whole Person Impairment thresholds (25% from 1 July 2026, rising to 27% in 2027 and 28% by 2029), the 130-week cap on weekly payments for primary psychological injury (down from up to 260 weeks), the single principal-assessment process for permanent impairment, the fixed employer excess applying to policies issued or renewed from 4pm 30 June 2026, the 1.99% Nominal Insurer premium-target freeze locked across 2026-27 and 2027-28 with Workers Compensation Industry Classification rates held flat and the minimum premium held at $240, and the section 26A enforceable psychosocial codes of practice. No new NSW regulator or tribunal release surfaced: no fresh Personal Injury Commission decision, Industrial Relations Commission determination on 'relevant conduct', SafeWork NSW prosecution or IRO release appeared in the last 24 hours, and the Personal Injury Commission continues to operationalise the changes without a citable new determination.
